goal: Phase 4 (never-signal-self) of campaign register-skill-and-harden: no code path in the factory can signal the process group it runs in, and no test names the test process itself as a controller or invocation the code may terminate -- the mechanism that killed the whole test runner with SIGKILL under load three times across two campaigns. Spec: docs/campaigns/register-skill-and-harden/spec/SPEC.md.

taskPacket.objective: terminateControllerGroup, terminateCoordinatorGroup and invocationOwned refuse a pid that is this process or its parent, and every test fixture that needs a live controller or invocation spawns a detached probe instead of naming process.pid, so the supervise, heartbeat, chain and process tests can never kill the test runner's own group.
instructions: Evidence (measured 2026-09-16 with a preload that logged every process.kill to a negative pid during a full test/engine/ run): the runner `node --test test/engine/` died with SIGKILL, exit null, at about 90 s into the suite in three separate full-suite runs across two campaigns, always under load, never in isolation. test/engine/supervise.test.mjs writes controller locks as `{pid: process.pid, processStartToken: processStartToken(process.pid)}` (liveLock and three inline copies) and calls superviseRun with `intervalSec: 0.001` and no injected `terminate`; when the heartbeat check breaches under load, superviseRun calls the real terminateControllerGroup, which -- with the pid alive and its token matching -- sends SIGTERM then SIGKILL to `-process.pid`, the process group of the test file, which is the runner's group. test/engine/heartbeat.test.mjs:168, test/campaign/chain.test.mjs:185 (coordinator lock) and test/run/process.test.mjs:554-569 use the same pattern.

Code guard. In src/engine/supervise.mjs terminateControllerGroup: before anything else, if the lock's pid equals process.pid or process.ppid, return false and record one `controller_self_signal_refused` event line through the run's existing event sink (or a stderr line if the function has no sink), never a throw. In src/campaign/chain.mjs terminateCoordinatorGroup (the takeover path, kill(-pid)): the same refusal for process.pid / process.ppid. In src/engine/process-identity.mjs invocationOwned: an invocation whose pid is process.pid or process.ppid is never owned (a controller does not spawn itself), so signalInvocation and terminateInvocation stay silent for it. Keep the existing start-token and child-handle logic.

Fixtures. Replace every controller or invocation fixture that names process.pid where the code under test may terminate it with a detached probe: `spawn(process.execPath, ['-e', 'setInterval(() => {}, 1000)'], {detached: true, stdio: 'ignore'})` (unref it, record its pid and processStartToken(pid), kill its group in a finally). Files: test/engine/supervise.test.mjs (liveLock and the inline locks at ~183, ~322, ~634), test/engine/heartbeat.test.mjs (~168), test/campaign/chain.test.mjs (~185), test/run/process.test.mjs (the 'eperm-owner' case at ~569 needs a probe whose real token matches; the 'fabricated' cases at ~554-562 may keep process.pid because they assert false). test/run/lock.test.mjs and test/run/pricing.test.mjs name process.pid only for lock acquisition and cost records that nothing terminates; leave them.

Tests for the guard: terminateControllerGroup on a lock naming process.pid returns false, signals nothing (inject `kill` and assert it was not called) and records the refusal; the same for a lock naming process.ppid; terminateCoordinatorGroup likewise; invocationOwned({pid: process.pid, processGroupId: process.pid, processStartToken: processStartToken(process.pid)}) is false even though the token matches. Every existing assertion in the touched files keeps holding.

Run tsc and test/repo/source-shape.test.mjs yourself. Never run npm install in the worktree; never run the whole suite yourself; never run tests that start and terminate child processes (test/run/, test/engine/supervise, heartbeat, seal-before-kill, unfreezable, judge, resume, test/campaign/chain) -- your dsh sandbox cannot signal processes and they hang until the executor cap; the controller runs them as this node's verification. The controller runs supervise, heartbeat, chain and process tests three times each as this node's verification; a single failure fails the node.
decisions: A controller never signals its own or its parent's process group; the refusal is recorded, never thrown.
Fixtures that the code may terminate spawn a detached probe; process.pid stays only where nothing terminates it.
Proof is repetition under the controller (repeat 3 on each affected test file).
nonGoals: Do not change staleness thresholds, relaunch rules or the seal.
Do not add a new node state or error code beyond the one event string.

Never run npm install in the worktree; never run the whole suite yourself; never run tests that start and terminate child processes (test/run/, test/engine/supervise, heartbeat, seal-before-kill, unfreezable, judge, resume, test/campaign/chain) -- your dsh sandbox cannot signal processes and they hang until the executor cap; the controller runs them as this node's verification.
